items.title: Sub-Part 11: Even Attachment to Meditation Itself Is Still Defilement

items.zh: 第六增上王、染時染自取；於無染、不染，染者名愚夫。
items.en: The sixth is the sovereign — there is a time of defilement, and defilement by grasping for oneself; where there is no defilement, nothing is defiled; whoever is defiled is called a fool.

items.zh: 今此頌中，第六增上王者，謂心、意、識。若有已渡五暴流，未渡第六意暴流；爾時其心隨逐諸定所有愛味，故名染時。復有補特伽羅，於長夜染取為己有，於可愛法執藏不捨，是故說彼為染自取。貪名為染；因貪所生當來世苦，亦名為染。若染自取，於所染心不隨功用，攝受、遮止、修意對治作意故；如是彼心於現法中無有染污。於無染心，此染自取當來世中因彼諸苦，亦無有染。若有於彼隨作功用，而不攝受、亦不遮止、不修意對治作意故；依此苦因，長夜受苦。於此苦因不能遠離，故名愚夫。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂薄伽梵此中略示，遠離苦因所有勝利，及顯苦因能感自苦，是愚夫性。當知是名此中略義。
items.en: In this verse, 'the sixth, the sovereign' means mind, mentation and consciousness. Suppose someone has already crossed the five floods but has not yet crossed the sixth, the flood of the mind; then their mind follows the relishing of the concentrations, and so this is called 'a time of defilement'. Again, there is a person who for a long time has been defiled, grasping things as their own, holding on to agreeable things and not letting them go; therefore they are said to be 'defiled by grasping for oneself'. Greed is called defilement; the future suffering born from greed is also called defilement. If one who is defiled by grasping for oneself does not exert themselves in following the defiled mind, but restrains it, checks it and applies the attention that cultivates the mind's antidote, then that mind is not defiled here and now. For a mind without defilement, this defilement of grasping for oneself brings no defilement either through the sufferings it would cause in the future. But if someone exerts themselves in following it, and does not restrain it, does not check it and does not apply the attention that cultivates the mind's antidote, then, relying on this cause of suffering, they experience suffering for a long time. Because they cannot keep far from this cause of suffering, they are called a fool. Further, the meaning of what was said above will now be briefly set out. In this verse the Blessed One briefly shows the benefit of keeping far from the cause of suffering, and shows that it is the nature of a fool that the cause of suffering brings about one's own suffering. It should be understood that this is the summary meaning here.

items.title: Sub-Part 12: The Fortress of Bone That Locks Wholesome Roots Out

items.zh: 有城骨為墉，筋肉而塗飾；其中有貪、恚、慢、覆、所任持。
items.en: There is a city walled with bone, plastered over with sinew and flesh — and within it, craving and aversion, conceit and concealment, hold their ground.

items.zh: 今此頌中，所言城者，謂心、意、識。此城唯以骨充甎石，筋代繩絍，肉當塗漫，為形骸墉周匝圍繞。此城中有違害善說法毘柰耶所有善法，四種惡法之所任持。二是在家諸受欲者，謂貪與瞋。二是惡說法毘柰耶中而出家者，謂慢與覆。由著諸欲、悕求諸欲，與鄙穢行不相違背，於善說法及毘柰耶尚不信受，況當修善。恃惡說法而生憍慢，不能自然趣佛世尊、或弟子所；設佛世尊、或佛弟子由悲愍故，自往其所，然彼由覆、隨煩惱、纏染污其心，尚不如實發露己過，況能信解修諸善法。如是當知，於彼善說法毘柰耶相應善法二種心城皆不能入，何況復能取為己有。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂薄伽梵此中略示，在家、出家總由四種雜染因緣，失壞善說法毘柰耶。當知是名此中略義。
items.en: In this verse, 'city' means mind, mentation and consciousness. This city has only bones for its bricks and stones, sinews in place of ropes and cords, and flesh for its plaster; the frame of the body is the wall that surrounds it on every side. Within this city, four evil qualities that oppose all the wholesome qualities of the well-proclaimed Dharma and Vinaya hold their ground. Two belong to householders who enjoy sense pleasures: greed and anger. Two belong to those who have gone forth in a badly proclaimed Dharma and Vinaya: conceit and concealment. Because the former are attached to sense pleasures and seek sense pleasures, and do not turn away from base conduct, they do not even accept the well-proclaimed Dharma and Vinaya with faith, let alone cultivate what is good. The latter, relying on a badly proclaimed Dharma, become arrogant and cannot of their own accord go to the Buddha, the World-Honoured One, or to his disciples. Even if the Buddha, the World-Honoured One, or a disciple of the Buddha, out of compassion, goes to them in person, their mind is defiled by concealment, a secondary affliction and entanglement, so that they do not even truthfully disclose their own faults, let alone have faith in and understanding of the wholesome qualities and cultivate them. So it should be understood that the wholesome qualities connected with the well-proclaimed Dharma and Vinaya cannot enter either of these two kinds of mind-city, still less be taken by them as their own. Further, the meaning of what was said above will now be briefly set out. In this verse the Blessed One briefly shows that householders and those gone forth alike, through four kinds of defiling conditions, lose and spoil the well-proclaimed Dharma and Vinaya. It should be understood that this is the summary meaning here.

items.title: Sub-Part 13: Drawing In Like a Tortoise, Rising Through the Absorptions

items.zh: 如龜藏支於自㲉，苾芻善攝意尋思；無所依止、不惱他，證般涅槃無所謗。
items.en: As a tortoise draws its limbs into its own shell, the monk skilfully draws in the mind's own rumination — relying on nothing, troubling no one — and realises final nirvāṇa, slandering nothing.

items.zh: 此頌所明，謂如有一，依初靜慮捨三惡尋。所謂欲尋、恚尋、害尋。又能棄捨初靜慮地諸善尋思，安住無尋無伺定中。如龜藏支於其自㲉，略攝尋思亦復如是。無尋無伺定者，應知此上乃至有頂。彼於此定正安住時，不生愛味。出已成就可愛樂法，調順柔和，易可共住，不惱有智同梵行者。又為智人同梵行者欣樂共住。又復成就無違諍法。彼由如是正方便故，於諸聖諦能入現觀，及得漏盡。彼於諸法不由他信，獲得善淨勝智見故，如實了知法真是法，毘柰耶真是毘柰耶。由如是知故，終不依止諸見顛倒，於法謗法，及於非法亦謗非法；終不顯示非法為法，法為非法，非毘柰耶為毘柰耶，或毘柰耶為非毘柰耶。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂薄伽梵此中略示，善說法者四種擾亂斷對治道。何等名為四種擾亂？一、染不染尋思擾亂，二、於勝定愛味擾亂，三、互相違諍訟擾亂，四、於正道誹謗擾亂。當知是名此中略義。
items.en: This verse explains the following. Someone, relying on the first meditation, abandons the three bad kinds of thought: thoughts of sense desire, thoughts of ill will and thoughts of harm. They are further able to give up even the wholesome thoughts of the stage of the first meditation and settle in concentration without applied and sustained thought. Like a tortoise drawing its limbs into its own shell, they likewise draw in their thinking. Concentration without applied and sustained thought should be understood to extend from here upwards to the peak of existence. While they are rightly settled in this concentration, they do not relish it. Having emerged from it, they possess agreeable and delightful qualities: they are tractable and gentle, easy to live with, and do not trouble wise companions in the holy life. Moreover, wise companions in the holy life delight in living with them. They also possess the quality of being free of contention. By such right effort they are able to enter direct realisation of the noble truths and attain the exhaustion of the outflows. They do not depend on faith in others concerning the teachings, because they have gained good, pure and superior knowledge and vision; they know as it really is that the Dharma is truly the Dharma and the Vinaya is truly the Vinaya. Knowing thus, they never rely on inverted views to slander the Dharma where there is Dharma, or to slander what is not the Dharma where there is no Dharma; they never present what is not the Dharma as the Dharma, or the Dharma as not the Dharma, what is not the Vinaya as the Vinaya, or the Vinaya as not the Vinaya. Further, the meaning of what was said above will now be briefly set out. In this verse the Blessed One briefly shows the path that counteracts and cuts off four kinds of disturbance for those of the well-proclaimed Dharma. What are the four kinds of disturbance? First, the disturbance of defiled and undefiled thinking; second, the disturbance of relishing superior concentration; third, the disturbance of mutual contention and quarrelling; fourth, the disturbance of slandering the right path. It should be understood that this is the summary meaning here.

blocks.text: Three short verses on the mind. All three explanations are **missing from Ru-Yi's translation**; the English column gives our own translation, and the commentary summarises them.
"The sixth is the sovereign: when defiled, it defiles by grasping for itself; where there is no defilement, nothing is defiled; whoever is defiled is called a fool."

The prose: the "sixth sovereign" is mind (心、意、識), the last of the six floods. One who has crossed the five sense floods but not the sixth still relishes meditation: "when defiled". Master Cháng Bǎi: craving for meditation is even stronger than sensual craving. Another holds pleasant things as "mine" through the long night. If one applies the antidote, the mind is not defiled now, and no future suffering follows. One who does not stays near the cause of suffering: "a fool".
"There is a city walled with bone, plastered with sinew and flesh, and within it craving and aversion, conceit and concealment, hold their ground."

The prose: the city is the mind, walled in a body of bone, sinew, and flesh. Four afflictions keep the good teaching out. Householders have **craving** and **aversion**; those who went forth under wrong teachings have **conceit** (proud of their doctrine, they will not come to the Buddha) and **concealment** (even when the Buddha comes to them out of compassion, they hide their faults). Master Cháng Bǎi: this applies also to Buddhist monastics who grow proud of a little concentration.
"As a tortoise draws its limbs into its shell, the monk draws in the mind's rumination, relying on nothing, troubling no one, and realises final nirvāṇa, slandering no one."

The prose: in the first dhyāna one gives up thoughts of desire, ill will, and harm; then even wholesome thoughts, entering concentration without examination (up to the peak of existence), drawn in "as a tortoise draws in its limbs". Master Cháng Bǎi: its head, tail, and four legs: six, like the six senses. One does not relish that concentration; emerging, one is gentle and easy to live with; one realises the truths and knows by oneself what is Dharma and Vinaya, and never calls Dharma non-Dharma.
In brief, the verse counters four disturbances: thoughts, attachment to concentration, quarrels, and slander of the path.

quiz.q: How do the two masters explain "the sixth, the sovereign"?
options: the sixth consciousness is a king
the king of the sixth heaven
Cháng Bǎi: sovereign means self-mastering and leading; Miào Jìng: "dominant" means powerful — the sixth, the mind base, governs the other five
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "king" means self-mastering, able to lead. Venerable Miào Jìng: "dominant" means having great power; "king" means mastery; the sixth, the mind base, governs the first five bases.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "when defiled" and "grasping for itself"?
options: craving and savouring meditation while practising it is "when defiled"; grasping that calm thought as self or mine is "grasping for itself"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: specifically, when practising meditation, craving and savouring it is "when defiled"; grasping the calm thought of meditation as self or mine — that craving is "grasping for itself."

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi compare craving for meditation with sensual craving?
options: stronger — those with concentration have strong minds, so meditative craving is hard to give up
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: craving for meditation is even stronger than sensual craving; those with concentration have very strong minds, and meditative craving is not easy to give up. He adds that one attached to meditation is still a foolish ordinary being within saṃsāra.

quiz.q: What does Master Cháng Bǎi say the first half, "a city walled with bone, plastered with sinew and flesh," stands for?
options: a being's mental and physical body
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "a city walled with bone, plastered over with sinew and flesh" is a simile for a being's mental body and physical body.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng define 覆 (concealment) in "conceit and concealment hold their ground"?
options: hypocrisy — hiding the truth and showing another face
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: concealment means hypocrisy — hiding the truth and displaying another face. Master Cháng Bǎi: concealment is the affliction of hiding one's wrongdoing.

quiz.q: How many "limbs" does the tortoise draw in, per the two masters?
options: six — head, tail, and four legs
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the tortoise has six parts — head, tail, and four legs — and draws all six into its shell. Venerable Miào Jìng: one head, four feet, plus a tail — six in all.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "relying on nothing"?
options: having no savouring or attached mind — savouring is "relying"; now there is none
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: if there is a savouring mind, an attached mind, that is called relying; now there is no reliance.
